reference: The onboarding flow needs to handle three separate permission prompts, and they all behave differently, which is annoying. Microphone access is the standard one that pops a system dialog immediately. Accessibility is the one where macOS just silently denies you until the user goes into System Settings and flips the toggle manually. And then Input Monitoring is the one nobody remembers exists until the global hotkey doesn't fire. What I think we should do is detect all three up front on first launch, show a single checklist screen with a green tick next to each one as it gets granted, and just poll every second or so to update it, because there's no callback for the accessibility one anyway.
